scope.summary: The old target needs an update. Both changed print depth checks apply to constructible cJSON trees, but every tree the target prints comes from a parser that rejects the depth needed to reach either check. The supplied scope is resolved.

assessments.reason: The new array print guard rejects an array encountered at depth 1000. A chain of 1001 arrays can be built with the public constructors and add operation, but the target prints only parser-produced trees; parsing rejects the 1001st container.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The parser rejects an array when its current depth reaches the same limit.
Appending an array child has no depth guard, so a deeper tree is a supported constructible print input.
The source default sets the nesting limit to 1000.

assessments.reason: The new object print guard rejects an object encountered at depth 1000. A chain of 1001 objects can be built through the public object operations, but the target prints only parser-produced trees; parsing rejects the 1001st container.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The parser rejects an object when its current depth reaches the same limit.
Adding an object child has no depth guard, so a deeper tree is a supported constructible print input.
The source default sets the nesting limit to 1000.

build.reason: The supplied recipe builds the static cJSON library and links the read target against it; the old entry uses declarations supplied by cJSON.h. This is a static recipe assessment, not a claimed build result.

evidence.dependency_reason: The harness build script delegates to this project recipe.
The old entry includes cJSON.h and supplies the fuzz entry point.

input.reason: The entry admits finite NUL-terminated payloads after four binary flags, and passes the payload as a C string with the selected termination option to the parser.

evidence.dependency_reason: The parser derives its length from the supplied C string and delegates with the termination option.

lifecycle.reason: On ordinary successful allocation paths, the target releases printed text, the optional writable minify copy, and the parsed tree. The source uses default malloc/free hooks and deletes child trees.

evidence.dependency_reason: The default allocation and deallocation hooks match the target's free calls.
cJSON_Delete releases parsed children and their owned storage.

control_flow.reason: The entry reaches all three print variants after a successful parse, and they dispatch arrays and objects to the changed functions. Their new rejection checks cannot be reached because the target never constructs or mutates the parsed tree and parsing enforces the same depth limit.

evidence.dependency_reason: The shared print dispatcher routes array and object items to the changed functions.
The array rejection requires depth 1000 before entering that array.
The object rejection requires depth 1000 before entering that object.
Parsing prevents the additional array depth needed by either print guard.
Parsing prevents the additional object depth needed by either print guard.

blockers.requirement: Make the supported rejection of a constructible array at print depth 1000 reachable from the read target.
blockers.target_route: Four valid flag bytes and a NUL-terminated JSON payload → cJSON_ParseWithOpts → one of cJSON_PrintBuffered, cJSON_Print, or cJSON_PrintUnformatted → print_value → print_array.
blockers.failure_condition: A finite chain of 1001 arrays is constructible and reaches the new print_array false return when printed directly. The old target cannot supply it: its parser rejects the 1001st container, and the entry prints only the parser result.
blockers.alternative_paths: All selected print variants use print_value. Neither flag choices, permitted trailing input, nor the later minify call construct or deepen the tree.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The public constructor creates an array node for the finite deep-tree witness.
The public add operation attaches each child without a depth restriction.
Parsing rejects an array once the input depth reaches the limit.
All print variants dispatch array and object values through print_value.

blockers.requirement: Make the supported rejection of a constructible object at print depth 1000 reachable from the read target.
blockers.target_route: Four valid flag bytes and a NUL-terminated JSON payload → cJSON_ParseWithOpts → one of cJSON_PrintBuffered, cJSON_Print, or cJSON_PrintUnformatted → print_value → print_object.
blockers.failure_condition: A finite chain of 1001 nested objects is constructible and reaches the new print_object false return when printed directly. The old target cannot supply it: its parser rejects the 1001st container, and the entry prints only the parser result.
blockers.alternative_paths: All selected print variants use print_value. Neither flag choices, permitted trailing input, nor the later minify call construct or deepen the tree.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The public constructor creates an object node for the finite deep-tree witness.
The public add operation attaches each named child without a depth restriction.
Parsing rejects an object once the input depth reaches the limit.
All print variants dispatch array and object values through print_value.
